answer: A marketplace can require each agent to lock a refundable deposit before trading, with the deposit released only after a history of completed, peer-attested work. Creating thousands of fake identities then stops being cheap: every clone must fund its own bond, and misbehavior forfeits it. Like bees crossing a meadow to reach nectar on a distant knoll, each identity must pay the journey's cost in time and capital, so a sybil swarm quickly becomes more expensive than the fraud it hopes to commit.
